To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Cadomian metasandstone and micaschists of Corsica are sourced from a Cadomian island arc that was built on a Meso-Paleo-proterozoic crust; (2) the Ordovician “Ciuttone” conglomerate was sourced from an island arc that evolved in the late Ediacaric Cadomian realm and that the Corsica island arc was detached from the Cadomian arc of southern France in the early Ordovician

Corsica is an outlier of Cadomian metasandstones and Ordovician conglomerate and sandstone, that the metasediments contain detrital zirs that are mostly Ediacaran in age and that the Ordovician conglomerates and sandstone were deposited in the Cadomia peripheral realm, and that they contain detrital grains that are exclusively Ediacaran in origin.
the Corsican Cadomian metasandstones and Ordovician siliciclasties were derived from Cadomian island arcs and that these were sourced from both juvenile and reworked crustal components.

the provenance of Cadomian metasadiments and Ordovican sandstone from Corscia.
the paleogeography of the Cadomio-Ordovician Corsica.
the Cadomian orogenic cycle in Corsica and the paleogeographic setting of the island during the Ediacaran and Ordovician.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Corsican metasediments are Cadomian and that the overlying Ordvician sandstone was deposited in a Cadomian peripheral arc setting.
the Cadomian domain was not a simple collage of Avalonian and Gondwanaan crustal blocks but rather an amalgam of various exotic crustal blocks, juvenile arcs, and reactivated Cadomian arcs.
Corsica was part of a peripheral Cadomian arc that was detached from the Variscan orogen during the Alpine orogeny.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Corsica Cadomian metase-diments were derived from a Cadomian basin that was located in the vicinity of the Gondwanan margin, while the Corsica Ordvician sandstone was derived from an Ediacaran arc that was located at the Cadomian periphery.
the Corsican metasedimentary sequence and overlying Ordovicain sandstone were deposited on a Cadomian arc that evolved in the peripheral domain of the Cadomia orogen.
the Cadomian terrane of Corsica was part of the Gondwane continent during the Ediacaran, but it became isolated from it by the end of the Ordovian.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cadomian orogenic realm was a composite of various terranes with distinct crustal histories.
